craft_notes: Sthāyin: witness-awe (the body testifies; Timirodghāṭana's own list). Sanskrit first: onset-signs (thrill, tears, yawn, faltering voice), deep-signs (burst knots, divine touch), crown (drops throbbing from navel) → L4 triplet: onset line 1, deep line 2, crown line 3 (the verse's own three breaths). Rows: row 2 (each sign kept whole — never split a symptom). Rupture: dash after 'crossing' — transmission named, body released; second dash-colon before the crown. Close: end-weight on the shrine ('navel-shrine' — kandas as holy place). Minimal pass: 'uplifted' for romaharṣa (hair-risen singable); 'hall' cut; giro 'ntaḥ kept literal ('from within'). Read aloud: line 1 quickens (fall/begun short), line 2 deepens (within/divine long), line 3 throbs (throbbing/shrine). Rejected: clinical terms ('piloerection/lacrimation') — killed: body-signs sung, not diagnosed; smoothing the uncertain giro — killed at L0 (literal kept, flagged).

lines: At the crossing — hair uplifted, tears that fall, yawns begun,
the voice faltering from within, knots burst, the touch divine —
l4.sanskrit_cite: yat saṃkrāntau romaharṣo 'srupāto jṛmbhārambho gadgadā gīr giro 'ntaḥ / granthisphoṭaḥ sparśadivyapraharṣo binduspandā nābhikandāt sphuranti

c1_essence: Transmission's body-signature: thrill, tears, yawning, faltering inner voices.
